clue.text: Iron lady's hat

parts.note: Fe is the chemical symbol for iron
Dora is a woman's name, standing in for any lady; the 's is a link

explanation.surface: A remark about the hat worn by the Iron Lady, Margaret Thatcher.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Iron lady' conjures Margaret Thatcher; the solver must split the phrase into an element symbol and a woman's name.
explanation.definitionFit: A fedora is a soft felt hat with a creased crown and brim.

clue.text: Retreat when summer has ended

explanation.walkthrough: In the US the clock change is remembered as 'spring forward, fall back'; fall is autumn.
explanation.definitionFit: To fall back is to withdraw, and at the end of summer time the clocks go back in the autumn, which Americans call fall.

clue.text: After going round the Philippines poor Gordon is flagging

indicators.note: the rearranged name goes round the abbreviation, enclosing it
poor signals the name is in a bad way, its letters jumbled

parts.note: PI stands for Philippine Islands

explanation.surface: Poor Gordon is wilting after a trip around the Philippines.
explanation.walkthrough: 'poor' jumbles the name into DROONG, which 'After going round' wraps about the islands' abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Drooping and flagging both mean sagging or losing energy.

clue.text: Promotional tour offers way to exhibit

parts.note: a road is a way
to exhibit is to show

explanation.surface: A promotional tour gives a way to put something on display.
explanation.definitionFit: A roadshow is a touring publicity event or broadcast.

clue.text: Odds on the second one causing a splash

parts.note: SP is starting price, the betting odds on a horse
the latter is the second of two things mentioned

explanation.surface: A gambler notes the odds on the second runner, which made a big impression.
explanation.walkthrough: SP, the starting price, is the horse-racing term for the odds at the off.
explanation.definitionFit: To splatter is to spray liquid about, making a splash.

clue.text: Something one has on buying a house

explanation.walkthrough: Taking possession is the legal moment a house buyer is given the keys.
explanation.definitionFit: A possession is an owned item, and a buyer takes possession of a property once the purchase completes.

clue.text: Always carried clothing, however fatigued

indicators.note: carried shows the word for always holding the clothing inside it

parts.note: ay (or aye) is an old word for always
wear means clothing, as in menswear

explanation.surface: Someone always lugged clothes about, yet felt tired.
explanation.walkthrough: 'carried' has AY hold WEAR: A-WEAR-Y. AY for ever is poetic and dialect usage.
explanation.definitionFit: Aweary is a poetic word for tired out.

clue.text: A lot of players set off to Peru

indicators.note: set off suggests departing but signals the letters being set out afresh

explanation.surface: A group of actors departs for Peru.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set off' turns TO PERU into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A troupe is a company of touring performers, a lot in the sense of a group.

clue.text: I had to enter arena on a horse

indicators.note: to enter means the contraction goes inside the arena word

parts.note: a ring is an arena, as in a circus ring
I'd is the contraction of I had

explanation.surface: Someone had to go into the arena mounted on a horse.
explanation.definitionFit: Riding means being mounted on and controlling a horse.

clue.text: A simpleton returned with hard, rough sponge

indicators.note: returned means the words a simpleton are read backwards

parts.note: a fool is a simpleton
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: A fool comes back holding a hard, coarse bath sponge.
explanation.definitionFit: A loofah is the dried fibrous gourd used as a scrubbing sponge.

clue.text: Radio-set broadcast from a minor planet

indicators.note: broadcast suggests radio but signals the letters scattered and reformed

explanation.surface: A radio set picks up a transmission from a small planet.
explanation.definitionFit: An asteroid is a small rocky body orbiting the sun, also called a minor planet.

clue.text: Circuitous way to purchase visa, it's said

indicators.note: it's said marks a word that sounds like the phrase rather than being spelt as it

parts.note: to purchase is to buy, and a visa is a pass

explanation.surface: Advice on a roundabout route to getting a travel permit.
explanation.definitionFit: A bypass is a road that skirts round a town, an indirect route.

clue.text: A turtle penny found in the country

indicators.note: found in means the coin's letter is located inside the land word

parts.note: terrain is country in the sense of land

explanation.surface: A turtle and a penny are discovered out in the countryside.
explanation.definitionFit: A terrapin is a small freshwater turtle.

clue.text: Injury suffered by 1000 pilots during exercise

annotationWithheld.why: Injury suffered by 1000 pilots during exercise (10): wordplay gives M + P(AIRMEN)T = MPAIRMENT; the leading I of IMPAIRMENT has no source in the clue as held (perhaps 'one thousand' originally), and no search found the printed clue.
annotationWithheld.clue: Injury suffered by 1000 pilots during exercise

clue.text: Anglican wants to study procedure first

parts.note: to con is to study, an old use
form is procedure, as in correct form
1st, with the 1 read as the letter I, is first

explanation.surface: A churchman insists on reading up on procedure before anything else.
explanation.walkthrough: 1ST is written with I standing in for the numeral 1.
explanation.definitionFit: Historically a conformist was one who complied with the Church of England, as opposed to a nonconformist.

clue.text: Allowed a tour to proceed without restriction

parts.note: let means allowed
a, meaning one, is I in Roman numerals
a trip is a tour

explanation.surface: A tour was permitted to go ahead unhindered.
explanation.definitionFit: To let it rip is an idiom for letting something go at full speed with no restraint.

clue.text: Guide famous old orator to Tyneside

parts.note: Cicero was the great Roman orator
Tyneside, around Newcastle, is in the North East of England, NE

explanation.surface: A celebrated ancient speaker is directed to Newcastle's region.
explanation.walkthrough: Tyneside is the area around Newcastle upon Tyne in north-east England.
explanation.definitionFit: A cicerone is a guide who shows sightseers around, named after the eloquent Roman.

clue.text: About to bisect bug under the rose

indicators.note: to bisect means cutting the creature in two by sitting inside it

parts.note: an insect is a bug
re means about, concerning

explanation.surface: Someone is about to cut a beetle in half beneath a rose bush.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to bisect' cuts the bug after its fourth letter. 'Under the rose' translates Latin sub rosa, meaning confidentially.
explanation.definitionFit: Sub rosa, literally under the rose, means privately or confidentially.

clue.text: Ivanhoe ran out of a princely house

indicators.note: out signals the letters are put out of order

explanation.surface: Scott's hero Ivanhoe flees from a royal residence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges IVANHOERAN. The House of Hanover supplied British monarchs from 1714.
explanation.definitionFit: Hanoverian means belonging to the royal dynasty of Hanover, a princely German line.

clue.text: People support a copper showing insight

indicators.note: in a down answer the supporting piece sits beneath what it holds up

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper
men are people

explanation.surface: Folk back a policeman who shows good judgement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'copper' looks like a policeman but is the metal, CU; in a down clue MEN supporting A CU goes underneath.
explanation.definitionFit: Acumen is shrewdness, the ability to judge quickly and well.

clue.text: Small motor ahead of Jack is a beetle

indicators.note: ahead of places the vehicle before the sailor

parts.note: a motor is a car
jack and AB (able seaman) both mean a sailor

explanation.surface: A little car out in front of a man named Jack turns out to be a bug.
explanation.definitionFit: The scarab is a dung beetle, sacred in ancient Egypt.

clue.text: Harry is a very musical pupil

parts.note: assai is the Italian musical direction for very, as in allegro assai
L is a learner, as on L-plates

explanation.surface: Harry is described as a highly musical student.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Harry' looks like a name but is a verb, to harass. L-plates mark learner drivers in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: To harry is to attack repeatedly, the same as to assail.

clue.text: Vulgar mate certain to be arrogant

parts.note: cock is a slangy British term of address for a friend or mate
sure means certain

explanation.surface: A coarse friend is bound to be full of himself.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wotcher, cock' is old Cockney for 'hello, mate'.
explanation.definitionFit: Cocksure means overconfident to the point of arrogance.

clue.text: Bishop and I lead army corps from ship

indicators.note: lead puts the first pieces in front of the corps

parts.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop
REME is the Royal Electrical and Mechanical Engineers, a British Army corps

explanation.surface: A bishop and I head an army unit off a vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: REME is the British Army's corps of Royal Electrical and Mechanical Engineers.
explanation.definitionFit: A bireme is an ancient galley with two banks of oars.

clue.text: She viewed a market surrounding French station

indicators.note: surrounding means the market word encloses the station

parts.note: a mart is a market
gare is French for railway station

explanation.surface: A woman looks at a market built around a French railway station.
explanation.definitionFit: Margaret is a woman's name, so it fits a pronoun standing for a female.

clue.text: Protection for Russian leader in romantic intrigue

indicators.note: in places the leading letter inside the love affair

parts.note: an amour is a love affair, especially a secret one

indicators.note: leader signals the first letter of the word Russian

explanation.surface: A Russian leader is shielded while caught up in an affair.
explanation.definitionFit: Armour is a protective covering, as worn by knights.

clue.text: No commoners display high-mindedness

explanation.walkthrough: 'display' is a link between the two senses.
explanation.definitionFit: The aristocracy are by definition not commoners, and the word also means moral excellence or nobleness of character.

clue.text: Optimistic conductor raises his baton thereupon

explanation.walkthrough: The second sense describes the upward stroke a conductor makes before the downbeat.
explanation.definitionFit: Upbeat means cheerful, and in music it is the unaccented beat, signalled by an upward stroke of the baton.
